content.text:
Generate an SVG of an octopus chef at a ramen booth

Deliver the result as image and/or video files, working in the current directory.
- Save the finished files in ./output/. Only what is in ./output/ is published as the result, so
  ./output/ holds those finished image/video files and nothing else.
- Formats: images as .png, .jpg, .webp, .gif or .svg; videos as .mp4 or .webm. At most 8 files,
  each under 2 MB; videos at most 10 seconds.
- Tools available on this machine: python3 3.15.0 (standard library only), node 26.12.0 (no npm packages), ffmpeg 9.0.2, ffprobe 9.0.2. Don't install packages or download anything.
- Keep the code you write to make the files in the working directory (its root, or a subdirectory
  like ./src/, but not in ./output/): it's published as the source. Delete intermediate files such
  as rendered frames when you're done.
- Only create or edit files inside the current directory.
- Finish with a short summary of what you made.

import CoreText
import Foundation

func svgFor(text: String, fontName: String, size: CGFloat, tracking: CGFloat) -> (String, Double, Double) {
    let font = CTFontCreateWithName(fontName as CFString, size, nil)
    let ps = CTFontCopyPostScriptName(font) as String
    fputs("font \(fontName) -> \(ps)\n", stderr)
    let attrs: [NSAttributedString.Key: Any] = [
        .font: font,
        .kern: tracking
    ]
    let astr = NSAttributedString(string: text, attributes: attrs)
    let line = CTLineCreateWithAttributedString(astr)
    var ascent: CGFloat = 0
    var descent: CGFloat = 0
    let width = CGFloat(CTLineGetTypographicBounds(line, &ascent, &descent, nil))
    var d = ""
    let runs = CTLineGetGlyphRuns(line) as! [CTRun]
    for run in runs {
        let n = CTRunGetGlyphCount(run)
        var glyphs = [CGGlyph](repeating: 0, count: n)
        var positions = [CGPoint](repeating: .zero, count: n)
        CTRunGetGlyphs(run, CFRange(location: 0, length: n), &glyphs)
        CTRunGetPositions(run, CFRange(location: 0, length: n), &positions)
        let runAttrs = CTRunGetAttributes(run) as NSDictionary
        let runFont = runAttrs[kCTFontAttributeName as NSAttributedString.Key] ?? runAttrs[kCTFontAttributeName] 
        let ctFont = runFont as! CTFont
        for i in 0..<n {
            guard let gp = CTFontCreatePathForGlyph(ctFont, glyphs[i], nil) else { continue }
            let pos = positions[i]
            gp.applyWithBlock { elem in
                let e = elem.pointee
                let pts = e.points
                func p(_ k: Int) -> String {
                    let x = pts[k].x + pos.x
                    let y = -(pts[k].y + pos.y)
                    return String(format: "%.2f %.2f", x, y)
                }
                switch e.type {
                case .moveToPoint: d += "M\(p(0))"
                case .addLineToPoint: d += "L\(p(0))"
                case .addQuadCurveToPoint: d += "Q\(p(0)) \(p(1))"
                case .addCurveToPoint: d += "C\(p(0)) \(p(1)) \(p(2))"
                case .closeSubpath: d += "Z"
                default: break
                }
            }
        }
    }
    return (d, Double(width), Double(ascent))
}

The crescent moon is enlarged to radius 48 at (100, 72), leaving a 36-pixel gap above the awning. It stays clear of the center hat area. A starfield is being added to the upper sky, with coordinates chosen to avoid both the moon and the hat.

Star coordinates are finalized with a few faint side-margin dots. A bokeh glow is being added behind the booth, using amber and red soft spots at reduced opacity.

The apron straps are now defined as thick strokes with round caps in #FFF8F0, placed behind the head and shadowed by a wider #E5D7C6 stroke. A warm pool on the ground is also being added to the scene.

The apron straps are drawn as curved bezier paths that connect to the bib behind the head. Armhole ellipses will be added to the bib. A small cup of green onions will sit on the counter next to the bottles.

The first render will stay minimal to avoid a muddy image. Core elements are prioritized: sky, moon, stars, awning, text, interior, menu, shelf, noren, octopus chef with hat and apron, eight tentacles, counter, pot with broth and bubbles, bowl with toppings, chopsticks, bottles, steam, and ground. Extra details like the green onion cup will be added only if the scene feels empty.

The spiral ribbon will be simplified to a gentle comma-shaped curl with 0.55 to 0.75 turns. This prevents self-intersection and keeps the dorsal highlight clean at this scale.

The showcase tentacle tip is set to 0.7 turns with a radius of 32 pixels, while the wave tip uses 0.65 turns and a radius of 24 pixels for a friendly beckoning curl. Sucker colors are finalized: skin fill #F07A68, outer ring #E98B80, mid-tone #C44E52, inner highlight #F6D0C8, and a white dot.

Suckers are being refined with a three-tier color scheme: a light rim, a darker cup interior, and a deep hole. Their size scales to 26% of the tentacle width with a 2.15x spacing. A staggered two-row layout is being drafted for the spiral ribbon.

The staggered sucker layout is being implemented with a distance-based sampler. It steps along the tentacle curve, measures segment length, and places the first row of suckers at 90% of the tentacle width, offset slightly along the normal vector. The second row is staggered by half the spacing distance to create the two-tier curl.

The staggered sucker layout is now fully implemented with distance-based sampling and a second row offset along the normal vector. A ventral lighter overlay is being considered, but an inner ribbon is preferred over a semi-transparent ellipse.

The inner ribbon is dropped from the first version to save time. Dorsal edge highlights will use a pale pink stroke and a subtle red shadow instead. The code is now being written with careful string formatting.

The menu board is being drawn with a dark wood frame and a light inner border. It will display four ramen items with prices. A red stamp on the bottom-right corner was considered but set aside to avoid colliding with the octopus head.

Dotted leaders will connect each menu item name to its price. The word MENU stays in white, and the stamp idea is dropped. Shelf bowls are being placed at y=458 across three positions.

Mini bowls are being drawn as white ellipses with a blue rim band. One stack will show three nested bowls at one position and two singles elsewhere. A red lacquer bowl stack is also planned. Interior plank lines and a post highlight will be added. A hook and towel with a red stripe will hang from the counter front on the right.

The stall feet are two dark wood blocks at the bottom of the posts, slightly wider than the posts themselves. The ground is a dark warm band from y=1148 to 1200 with a lighter ellipse overlay. The feet overlap the ground.

The skirt hem will be a 10-pixel cream band with a 6-pixel red stripe above it. A tentacle will curl across this seam for a graphic finish. The generator will be written as a single file and executed immediately after writing. The script will include a default `--out` path.

The tentacle path is built in four stages: Catmull spline interpolation, spiral insertion, resampling to 4-pixel intervals, then width and normal calculation. A 300-pixel tentacle yields roughly 75 points. SVG line length limits are not a concern at this scale.

Minimum widths are being set so tentacle curls remain visible. Most tips will be 6 pixels wide, with the wave tip at 7 and the showcase end at 8. The spiral curl tapers naturally from the base width to this minimum, keeping the spiral visible without extra logic.

The spiral curl is confirmed to sit at the very end of each tentacle, so it naturally tapers into the minimum tip width without extra logic. Its arc length is only about 57 pixels, keeping the curve compact. A potential bug in the semi-cap normal calculation is being flagged for review. Edge strokes on the filled tentacles will use round caps.

The SVG will be 1200 by 1200 pixels with a viewBox of 0 0 1200 1200. Filters will be attached to the group element rather than individual paths. A module docstring and XML declaration will be included in the generator file.

The chashu spiral will be a simple arc with an inner darker crescent. Nori texture is three horizontal lighter lines. The egg yolk gets a radial gradient. Broth gradient and oil ellipses are added. A teardrop droplet sits under the longest noodle. Three small scallions fall from tentacle E between its tip and the bowl.

The falling scallions are placed at (890, 830), (870, 860), and (910, 850). Three green-to-white gradient scallion stalks will extend from the curl tip.

Scallion stalks will be drawn as thick green lines with a white base. Small rounded rectangles will represent the cut rings and diagonal pieces.

Scallion pieces are now drawn as rotated rounded rectangles with a green body and white base. The soy bottle is being sketched with a rounded body, neck, spout, cream label, and red accent. A Rayu jar is also being drafted.

A soft blur filter will be defined in the SVG defs for contact shadows. A helper function will draw dimmed ellipses beneath the bowl, pot, and bottles to create a subtle ground shadow.

The steam filter blur is set to 6 and the glow filter to 14. A yellow lantern behind the stall will pulse with an animated opacity. The lantern body is a wide oval with a slight middle bulge. It has a black top cap and a short gold tassel. A dark string hangs from the cap to the awning.

The left lantern is placed at x=172, just inside the stall and in front of the left noren. It will cover the outer panel, so the mon will be moved to the inner panel.

The right lantern is placed at x=1030, covering the outer noren edge and the post. The mon will sit on the inner right panel at x=900. The vertical string at that x-coordinate might cross the RAMEN text, which ends near x=1032.

The lantern string starts at y=250, so it clears the RAMEN text. The wave tentacle curl is being shifted to (940, 480) to avoid the right lantern at x=1030.

The right lantern is moved to x=1064, hanging directly from the right post. The left lantern is placed at x=132, just in front of the left post. Both sit symmetrically on the outer edges of the stall. The TAKO text starts near x=206, leaving a clear gap before the left lantern ends at 170. The awning spans x=64 to 1136, with its top edge at y=158 and side edges at y=246.

TAKO text is centered at x=330 with baseline y=222. RAMEN text is centered at x=860 with the same baseline. The awning top will curve upward 20 pixels at its center to form a gentle arch, while the hat sits directly over that peak.

The awning top is being tightened to a quadratic bezier curve with control point (600, 140) so the sides sit at y=162. Text baseline is set to 228 and side padding to 16 pixels.

The quadratic bezier curve places the awning top at roughly y=154 under both TAKO and RAMEN. The text baseline is y=228, so the 20-pixel padding holds on both sides.

The quadratic bezier peak is only about 11 pixels above the sides, so the arch will stay subtle and elegant rather than dramatic.

The awning arch is being raised to a 30-pixel peak at the center by setting the quadratic bezier control point to y=102. The midpoint then sits at y=132, leaving about 35 pixels of clearance above the TAKO text.

The hat top is fixed at y=100, so it pokes about 32 pixels above the awning arch peak. The bottom edge of the awning sags 15 pixels at its center, keeping the silhouette balanced and natural.

A cream piping stroke will trace the bottom curve, and a filled band will shade the underside. The hat pills are set to a 40 by 255 pixel rectangle spanning y=100 to y=355.

The hat pills are too tall and thin. A 40 by 255 pixel rectangle is extremely elongated for a toque. A shorter, wider crown would look better. But the awning peak sits at y=132, so the hat top must stay above that point. A 200 pixel height would leave only seven pixels of clearance, which is too subtle.

The hat will be wider than the awning peak so its sides merge with the stall while the center tip rises above it. The crown will stretch from y=88 to y=340, and five wide, overlapping puffy lobes will replace the thin pills to avoid looking like a candle.

The hat will use five plump pleats, each 78 pixels wide with a 39.5 pixel overlap. Heights will peak at the center and taper toward the sides, alternating warm white tones for a soft chef look. A tiny smile line and cheek will be added to the face, with the eyes made the most prominent feature.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Draw an octopus chef working a night-market ramen booth.

The illustration is a single SVG. Sign and menu lettering is outlined
(see glyphs.py) so it stays put without embedded fonts.

Run: python3 src/generate_octopus_ramen.py
"""

import math
import os
from pathlib import Path

from glyphs import GLYPHS

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
OUT = ROOT / "output" / "octopus-chef-ramen.svg"

W, H = 1200, 1200
DEBUG = os.environ.get("DEBUG") == "1"

# Locked stage geometry. Tweaked against raster previews.
HEAD = (600, 478, 162, 132)  # cx, cy, rx, ry
HAT_CX = 598
HAT_TOP = 96
HAT_BAND_Y = 348
BOWL_C = (804, 872)
BOWL_RX, BOWL_RY = 196, 74
POT_C = (308, 692)
POT_RX, POT_RY = 112, 42


def fmt(v):
    if isinstance(v, str):
        return v
    s = f"{float(v):.1f}"
    return s[:-2] if s.endswith(".0") else s


def poly(pts, close=True):
    if not pts:
        return ""
    cmds = [f"M{fmt(pts[0][0])} {fmt(pts[0][1])}"]
    cmds.extend(f"L{fmt(x)} {fmt(y)}" for x, y in pts[1:])
    if close:
        cmds.append("Z")
    return "".join(cmds)


def catmull(points, samples=12):
    if len(points) < 2:
        return list(points)
    p = [points[0]] + list(points) + [points[-1]]
    out = []
    for i in range(1, len(p) - 2):
        p0, p1, p2, p3 = p[i - 1], p[i], p[i + 1], p[i + 2]
        for s in range(samples):
            t = s / samples
            t2 = t * t
            t3 = t2 * t
            x = 0.5 * (
                (2 * p1[0])
                + (-p0[0] + p2[0]) * t
                + (2 * p0[0] - 5 * p1[0] + 4 * p2[0] - p3[0]) * t2
                + (-p0[0] + 3 * p1[0] - 3 * p2[0] + p3[0]) * t3
            )
            y = 0.5 * (
                (2 * p1[1])
                + (-p0[1] + p2[1]) * t
                + (2 * p0[1] - 5 * p1[1] + 4 * p2[1] - p3[1]) * t2
                + (-p0[1] + 3 * p1[1] - 3 * p2[1] + p3[1]) * t3
            )
            out.append((x, y))
    out.append(points[-1])
    return out


def resample(pts, step=4.2):
    if len(pts) < 2:
        return list(pts)
    seglen = []
    total = 0.0
    for i in range(1, len(pts)):
        L = math.hypot(pts[i][0] - pts[i - 1][0], pts[i][1] - pts[i - 1][1])
        seglen.append(L)
        total += L
    if total < step:
        return [pts[0], pts[-1]]
    out = [pts[0]]
    target = step
    seg_i = 0
    acc = 0.0
    while target < total - 0.01 and seg_i < len(seglen):
        while seg_i < len(seglen) and acc + seglen[seg_i] < target:
            acc += seglen[seg_i]
            seg_i += 1
        if seg_i >= len(seglen) or seglen[seg_i] < 1e-8:
            break
        local = (target - acc) / seglen[seg_i]
        x0, y0 = pts[seg_i]
        x1, y1 = pts[seg_i + 1]
        out.append((x0 + (x1 - x0) * local, y0 + (y1 - y0) * local))
        target += step
    out.append(pts[-1])
    return out


def append_spiral(pts, turns=0.7, radius=26, clockwise=True, samples=26):
    """Hook the tip into a tightening curl whose start tangent matches the arm."""
    if len(pts) < 2 or radius <= 1:
        return pts
    x1, y1 = pts[-1]
    x0, y0 = pts[-2]
    direction = math.atan2(y1 - y0, x1 - x0)
    sign = 1.0 if clockwise else -1.0
    raw = []
    for i in range(samples + 1):
        t = i / samples
        theta = sign * t * turns * math.tau
        r = radius * (1 - t * 0.86)
        raw.append((r * math.cos(theta) - radius, r * math.sin(theta)))
    tang = math.atan2(raw[1][1] - raw[0][1], raw[1][0] - raw[0][0])
    rot = direction - tang
    ca, sa = math.cos(rot), math.sin(rot)
    out = list(pts)
    for x, y in raw[1:]:
        out.append((x1 + x * ca - y * sa, y1 + x * sa + y * ca))
    return out


def normals(pts):
    n = len(pts)
    raw = []
    for i in range(n):
        if i == 0:
            dx = pts[1][0] - pts[0][0]
            dy = pts[1][1] - pts[0][1]
        elif i == n - 1:
            dx = pts[-1][0] - pts[-2][0]
            dy = pts[-1][1] - pts[-2][1]
        else:
            dx = pts[i + 1][0] - pts[i - 1][0]
            dy = pts[i + 1][1] - pts[i - 1][1]
        L = math.hypot(dx, dy) or 1.0
        raw.append((-dy / L, dx / L))
    fixed = [raw[0]]
    for i in range(1, n):
        nx, ny = raw[i]
        if nx * fixed[-1][0] + ny * fixed[-1][1] < 0:
            nx, ny = -nx, -ny
        fixed.append((nx, ny))
    cur = fixed
    for _ in range(2):
        nxt = [cur[0]]
        for i in range(1, n - 1):
            x = cur[i - 1][0] + cur[i][0] + cur[i + 1][0]
            y = cur[i - 1][1] + cur[i][1] + cur[i + 1][1]
            L = math.hypot(x, y) or 1.0
            nxt.append((x / L, y / L))
        nxt.append(cur[-1])
        cur = nxt
    return cur


def width_profile(n, base, tip, bulge=0.08):
    ws = []
    for i in range(n):
        t = i / (n - 1) if n > 1 else 0.0
        w = tip + (base - tip) * (1 - t) ** 0.76
        w *= 1 + bulge * math.sin(math.pi * t)
        ws.append(w)
    return ws


def semi_cap(tip, normal, width, forward=True, n=8):
    nx, ny = normal
    dx, dy = (ny, -nx) if forward else (-ny, nx)
    hw = width / 2
    pts = []
    for i in range(1, n):
        a = math.pi * i / n
        pts.append(
            (
                tip[0] + hw * (math.cos(a) * nx + math.sin(a) * dx),
                tip[1] + hw * (math.cos(a) * ny + math.sin(a) * dy),
            )
        )
    return pts


def ribbon_edges(pts, widths, norms):
    left, right = [], []
    for (x, y), (nx, ny), w in zip(pts, norms, widths):
        hw = w / 2
        left.append((x + nx * hw, y + ny * hw))
        right.append((x - nx * hw, y - ny * hw))
    cap = semi_cap(pts[-1], norms[-1], widths[-1], True)
    base = semi_cap(pts[0], norms[0], widths[0], False)
    outline = left + cap + list(reversed(right)) + list(reversed(base))
    return outline, left, right


def sucker_positions(pts, widths, norms, side, rows):
    found = []
    dist = 0.0
    next_at = max(8.0, widths[0] * 0.55)
    next_row2 = next_at + 9
    for i in range(1, len(pts) - 1):
        dist += math.hypot(pts[i][0] - pts[i - 1][0], pts[i][1] - pts[i - 1][1])
        t = i / (len(pts) - 1)
        w = widths[i]
        r = max(2.4, w * 0.268)
        spacing = max(r * 2.2, 7.5)
        nx, ny = norms[i]
        if 0.07 < t < 0.9 and dist >= next_at:
            found.append(
                (
                    pts[i][0] + side * nx * w * 0.04,
                    pts[i][1] + side * ny * w * 0.04,
                    r,
                )
            )
            next_at = dist + spacing
        if rows >= 2 and w > 18 and 0.12 < t < 0.86 and dist >= next_row2:
            r2 = r * 0.86
            found.append(
                (
                    pts[i][0] + side * nx * w * 0.30,
                    pts[i][1] + side * ny * w * 0.30,
                    r2,
                )
            )
            next_row2 = dist + max(r2 * 2.35, 8)
    return found


def sucker_mark(cx, cy, r):
    return (
        f'<circle cx="{fmt(cx)}" cy="{fmt(cy)}" r="{fmt(r)}" fill="#F3B2A6"/>'
        f'<circle cx="{fmt(cx)}" cy="{fmt(cy)}" r="{fmt(r * 0.70)}" fill="#D25A56"/>'
        f'<circle cx="{fmt(cx)}" cy="{fmt(cy)}" r="{fmt(r * 0.36)}" fill="#9E333C"/>'
        f'<circle cx="{fmt(cx - r * 0.28)}" cy="{fmt(cy - r * 0.30)}" r="{fmt(r * 0.16)}" fill="#fff" opacity="0.8"/>'
    )


def draw_tentacle(points, base, tip, fill, sucker_side=1, rows=1, spiral=None, bulge=0.08):
    pts = catmull(points, 11)
    if spiral:
        pts = append_spiral(pts, **spiral)
    pts = resample(pts, 4.0)
    if len(pts) < 4:
        return ""
    ws = width_profile(len(pts), base, tip, bulge)
    norms = normals(pts)
    outline, left, right = ribbon_edges(pts, ws, norms)
    dorsal = right if sucker_side > 0 else left
    ventral = left if sucker_side > 0 else right
    parts = [
        f'<path d="{poly(outline)}" fill="{fill}"/>',
        f'<path d="{poly(dorsal, False)}" fill="none" stroke="#FFD5CB" stroke-width="3.4" stroke-linecap="round" opacity="0.8"/>',
        f'<path d="{poly(ventral, False)}" fill="none" stroke="#A83840" stroke-width="2.4" stroke-linecap="round" opacity="0.4"/>',
    ]
    for cx, cy, r in sucker_positions(pts, ws, norms, sucker_side, rows):
        parts.append(sucker_mark(cx, cy, r))
    if DEBUG:
        parts.append(
            f'<path d="{poly(pts, False)}" fill="none" stroke="#00e5ff" stroke-width="1"/>'
        )
    return "".join(parts)


def text_glyph(key, x, baseline, fill, anchor="left", dx=0, dy=0, opacity=1):
    d, w, _a = GLYPHS[key]
    if anchor == "center":
        x -= w / 2
    elif anchor == "right":
        x -= w
    op = "" if opacity == 1 else f' opacity="{opacity}"'
    return (
        f'<path d="{d}" fill="{fill}" fill-rule="evenodd"{op} '
        f'transform="translate({fmt(x + dx)} {fmt(baseline + dy)})"/>'
    )


def ellipse(cx, cy, rx, ry, fill, extra=""):
    return (
        f'<ellipse cx="{fmt(cx)}" cy="{fmt(cy)}" rx="{fmt(rx)}" ry="{fmt(ry)}" '
        f'fill="{fill}"{extra}/>'
    )


def steam_wisp(cx, y0, height, width, bend):
    """Tapered vertical puff. y0 is the base; the wisp rises by `height`."""
    pts = []
    n = 18
    for i in range(n + 1):
        t = i / n
        y = y0 - height * t
        x = cx + math.sin(t * math.pi) * bend + math.sin(t * math.tau) * bend * 0.25
        pts.append((x, y))
    ws = [math.sin(i / n * math.pi) * width for i in range(n + 1)]
    ws[0] = 0.8
    ws[-1] = 0.6
    norms = normals(pts)
    outline, _, _ = ribbon_edges(pts, ws, norms)
    return poly(outline)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Scene
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def defs():
    return """

    # Crescent moon, upper left, clear of the awning.

        f"M{fmt(cx - rx)},{fmt(cy)} "

        f"Q{fmt(cx)},{fmt(cy + 28 * s)} {fmt(cx + 12 * s)},{fmt(cy + 22 * s)} "
        f"C{fmt(cx + 16 * s)},{fmt(cy + 22 * s)} {fmt(cx + rx)},{fmt(cy + 16 * s)} {fmt(cx + rx)},{fmt(cy)} Z"

    left = HAT_CX - total / 2
    factors = [0.84, 0.94, 1.0, 0.93, 0.82]

def _rim_band(cx, cy, rx, ry, thickness, near=True):
    rxi = rx - thickness
    ryi = max(6, ry - thickness * 0.72)
    if near:
        # Lower half: left --clockwise--> right, back along the inner edge.
        d = (
            f"M{fmt(cx - rx)},{fmt(cy)} A{fmt(rx)},{fmt(ry)} 0 0 1 {fmt(cx + rx)},{fmt(cy)} "
            f"L{fmt(cx + rxi)},{fmt(cy)} A{fmt(rxi)},{fmt(ryi)} 0 0 0 {fmt(cx - rxi)},{fmt(cy)} Z"
        )
        red = (
            f"M{fmt(cx - rxi + 2)},{fmt(cy + 2)} A{fmt(rxi - 2)},{fmt(ryi - 2)} 0 0 1 "
            f"{fmt(cx + rxi - 2)},{fmt(cy + 2)}"
        )
    else:
        d = (
            f"M{fmt(cx - rx)},{fmt(cy)} A{fmt(rx)},{fmt(ry)} 0 0 0 {fmt(cx + rx)},{fmt(cy)} "
            f"L{fmt(cx + rxi)},{fmt(cy)} A{fmt(rxi)},{fmt(ryi)} 0 0 1 {fmt(cx - rxi)},{fmt(cy)} Z"
        )
        red = (
            f"M{fmt(cx - rxi + 2)},{fmt(cy)} A{fmt(rxi - 2)},{fmt(max(4, ryi - 2))} 0 0 0 "
            f"{fmt(cx + rxi - 2)},{fmt(cy)}"
        )
    return (
        f'<path d="{d}" fill="#FFF8F0"/>'
        f'<path d="{red}" fill="none" stroke="#C4473A" stroke-width="2.4" opacity="0.85"/>'
    )


def _noodle_strand(x0, y, length, amp, waves, phase, sag, width, color):
    pts = []
    n = 22
    for i in range(n + 1):
        t = i / n
        x = x0 + length * t
        yy = y + math.sin(t * waves * math.tau + phase) * amp + math.sin(t * math.pi) * sag
        pts.append((x, yy))
    return (
        f'<path d="{poly(pts, False)}" fill="none" stroke="{color}" stroke-width="{fmt(width)}" '
        f'stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"/>'
    )

def _naruto(cx, cy):
    # Pink spiral fish cake, standing nearly face-on.
    pts = []
    turns, n = 2.15, 70
    for i in range(n + 1):
        t = i / n
        a = t * turns * math.tau
        r = 2 + t * 13
        pts.append((cx + r * math.cos(a), cy + r * math.sin(a) * 0.92))
    return (
        f'<ellipse cx="{fmt(cx)}" cy="{fmt(cy)}" rx="20" ry="18" fill="#FFFCFA" stroke="#F3C2D0" stroke-width="1"/>'
        f'<circle cx="{fmt(cx)}" cy="{fmt(cy)}" r="16" fill="none" stroke="#F4A2B8" stroke-width="3"/>'
        f'<path d="{poly(pts, False)}" fill="none" stroke="#F28BA8" stroke-width="3.2" stroke-linecap="round"/>'
    )

def lifted_noodles():
    """U-shaped strands pinched by the chopsticks, dripping back into the bowl."""
    tipx, tipy = 786, 778
    parts = []
    strands = [
        (-8, 6, 64, 2.0, "#E8D0A0", 6.4),
        (-2, 10, 96, 2.4, "#F8E7C4", 7.2),
        (4, 4, 118, 1.6, "#E2C890", 6.6),
        (0, 12, 78, 2.2, "#FFF3D8", 7.0),
        (6, 8, 102, 1.8, "#F3E0B0", 6.2),
        (-4, 2, 88, 2.6, "#EBD7A4", 7.4),
    ]
    for ox, oy, droop, wav, col, width in strands:
        pts = []
        n = 26
        x0, x1 = tipx - 7 + ox, tipx + 9 + ox
        y = tipy + oy
        for i in range(n + 1):
            t = i / n
            x = x0 + (x1 - x0) * t
            sag = math.sin(t * math.pi) * droop
            wave = math.sin(t * 6 * math.pi) * wav * math.sin(t * math.pi)
            pts.append((x, y + sag + wave))
        parts.append(
            f'<path d="{poly(pts, False)}" fill="none" stroke="{col}" stroke-width="{width}" '
            f'stroke-linecap="round"/>'
        )
    # Broth bead falling from the longest strand.
    dx, dy = tipx + 2, tipy + 104
    parts.append(
        f'<path d="M{fmt(dx)},{fmt(dy - 8)} C{fmt(dx - 5)},{fmt(dy - 2)} {fmt(dx - 4.5)},{fmt(dy + 5)} '
        f'{fmt(dx)},{fmt(dy + 8)} C{fmt(dx + 4.5)},{fmt(dy + 5)} {fmt(dx + 5)},{fmt(dy - 2)} {fmt(dx)},{fmt(dy - 8)} Z" '
        f'fill="#E39B2B"/>'
        f'<ellipse cx="{fmt(dx - 1.5)}" cy="{fmt(dy - 2)}" rx="1.6" ry="2.4" fill="#fff" opacity="0.65"/>'
    )
    return "".join(parts)

"""Draw an octopus chef working a night-market ramen booth.

The illustration is a single SVG. Sign and menu lettering is outlined

import math
import os
from pathlib import Path

def fmt(v):
    if isinstance(v, str):
        return v
    s = f"{float(v):.1f}"
    return s[:-2] if s.endswith(".0") else s


def poly(pts, close=True):
    if not pts:
        return ""
    cmds = [f"M{fmt(pts[0][0])} {fmt(pts[0][1])}"]
    cmds.extend(f"L{fmt(x)} {fmt(y)}" for x, y in pts[1:])
    if close:
        cmds.append("Z")
    return "".join(cmds)


def catmull(points, samples=12):
    if len(points) < 2:
        return list(points)
    p = [points[0]] + list(points) + [points[-1]]
    out = []
    for i in range(1, len(p) - 2):
        p0, p1, p2, p3 = p[i - 1], p[i], p[i + 1], p[i + 2]
        for s in range(samples):
            t = s / samples
            t2 = t * t
            t3 = t2 * t
            x = 0.5 * (
                (2 * p1[0])
                + (-p0[0] + p2[0]) * t
                + (2 * p0[0] - 5 * p1[0] + 4 * p2[0] - p3[0]) * t2
                + (-p0[0] + 3 * p1[0] - 3 * p2[0] + p3[0]) * t3
            )
            y = 0.5 * (
                (2 * p1[1])
                + (-p0[1] + p2[1]) * t
                + (2 * p0[1] - 5 * p1[1] + 4 * p2[1] - p3[1]) * t2
                + (-p0[1] + 3 * p1[1] - 3 * p2[1] + p3[1]) * t3
            )
            out.append((x, y))
    out.append(points[-1])
    return out


def resample(pts, step=4.2):
    if len(pts) < 2:
        return list(pts)
    seglen = []
    total = 0.0
    for i in range(1, len(pts)):
        L = math.hypot(pts[i][0] - pts[i - 1][0], pts[i][1] - pts[i - 1][1])
        seglen.append(L)
        total += L
    if total < step:
        return [pts[0], pts[-1]]
    out = [pts[0]]
    target = step
    seg_i = 0
    acc = 0.0
    while target < total - 0.01 and seg_i < len(seglen):
        while seg_i < len(seglen) and acc + seglen[seg_i] < target:
            acc += seglen[seg_i]
            seg_i += 1
        if seg_i >= len(seglen) or seglen[seg_i] < 1e-8:
            break
        local = (target - acc) / seglen[seg_i]
        x0, y0 = pts[seg_i]
        x1, y1 = pts[seg_i + 1]
        out.append((x0 + (x1 - x0) * local, y0 + (y1 - y0) * local))
        target += step
    out.append(pts[-1])
    return out


def append_spiral(pts, turns=0.7, radius=26, clockwise=True, samples=26):
    """Hook the tip into a tightening curl whose start tangent matches the arm."""
    if len(pts) < 2 or radius <= 1:
        return pts
    x1, y1 = pts[-1]
    x0, y0 = pts[-2]
    direction = math.atan2(y1 - y0, x1 - x0)
    sign = 1.0 if clockwise else -1.0
    raw = []
    for i in range(samples + 1):
        t = i / samples
        theta = sign * t * turns * math.tau
        r = radius * (1 - t * 0.86)
        raw.append((r * math.cos(theta) - radius, r * math.sin(theta)))
    tang = math.atan2(raw[1][1] - raw[0][1], raw[1][0] - raw[0][0])
    rot = direction - tang
    ca, sa = math.cos(rot), math.sin(rot)
    out = list(pts)
    for x, y in raw[1:]:
        out.append((x1 + x * ca - y * sa, y1 + x * sa + y * ca))
    return out


def normals(pts):
    n = len(pts)
    raw = []
    for i in range(n):
        if i == 0:
            dx = pts[1][0] - pts[0][0]
            dy = pts[1][1] - pts[0][1]
        elif i == n - 1:
            dx = pts[-1][0] - pts[-2][0]
            dy = pts[-1][1] - pts[-2][1]
        else:
            dx = pts[i + 1][0] - pts[i - 1][0]
            dy = pts[i + 1][1] - pts[i - 1][1]
        L = math.hypot(dx, dy) or 1.0
        raw.append((-dy / L, dx / L))
    fixed = [raw[0]]
    for i in range(1, n):
        nx, ny = raw[i]
        if nx * fixed[-1][0] + ny * fixed[-1][1] < 0:
            nx, ny = -nx, -ny
        fixed.append((nx, ny))
    cur = fixed
    for _ in range(2):
        nxt = [cur[0]]
        for i in range(1, n - 1):
            x = cur[i - 1][0] + cur[i][0] + cur[i + 1][0]
            y = cur[i - 1][1] + cur[i][1] + cur[i + 1][1]
            L = math.hypot(x, y) or 1.0
            nxt.append((x / L, y / L))

        cur = nxt
    return cur


def width_profile(n, base, tip, bulge=0.08):
    ws = []
    for i in range(n):
        t = i / (n - 1) if n > 1 else 0.0
        w = tip + (base - tip) * (1 - t) ** 0.76
        w *= 1 + bulge * math.sin(math.pi * t)
        ws.append(w)
    return ws


def semi_cap(tip, normal, width, forward=True, n=8):
    nx, ny = normal
    dx, dy = (ny, -nx) if forward else (-ny, nx)
    hw = width / 2
    pts = []
    for i in range(1, n):
        a = math.pi * i / n
        pts.append(
            (
                tip[0] + hw * (math.cos(a) * nx + math.sin(a) * dx),
                tip[1] + hw * (math.cos(a) * ny + math.sin(a) * dy),
            )
        )
    return pts


def ribbon_edges(pts, widths, norms):
    left, right = [], []
    for (x, y), (nx, ny), w in zip(pts, norms, widths):
        hw = w / 2
        left.append((x + nx * hw, y + ny * hw))
        right.append((x - nx * hw, y - ny * hw))
    cap = semi_cap(pts[-1], norms[-1], widths[-1], True)
    base = semi_cap(pts[0], norms[0], widths[0], False)
    outline = left + cap + list(reversed(right)) + list(reversed(base))
    return outline, left, right


def sucker_positions(pts, widths, norms, side, rows):
    found = []
    dist = 0.0
    next_at = max(8.0, widths[0] * 0.55)
    next_row2 = next_at + 9
    for i in range(1, len(pts) - 1):
        dist += math.hypot(pts[i][0] - pts[i - 1][0], pts[i][1] - pts[i - 1][1])
        t = i / (len(pts) - 1)
        w = widths[i]
        r = max(2.4, w * 0.268)
        spacing = max(r * 2.2, 7.5)
        nx, ny = norms[i]
        if 0.07 < t < 0.9 and dist >= next_at:
            found.append(
                (
                    pts[i][0] + side * nx * w * 0.04,
                    pts[i][1] + side * ny * w * 0.04,

        if rows >= 2 and w > 18 and 0.12 < t < 0.86 and dist >= next_row2:

            found.append(

                    pts[i][1] + side * ny * w * 0.30,
                    r2,

            )
            next_row2 = dist + max(r2 * 2.35, 8)
    return found


def sucker_mark(cx, cy, r):

        f'<circle cx="{fmt(cx - r * 0.28)}" cy="{fmt(cy - r * 0.30)}" r="{fmt(r * 0.16)}" fill="#fff" opacity="0.8"/>'

def draw_tentacle(points, base, tip, fill, sucker_side=1, rows=1, spiral=None, bulge=0.08):
    pts = catmull(points, 11)

        f'<path d="{poly(dorsal, False)}" fill="none" stroke="#FFD5CB" stroke-width="3.4" stroke-linecap="round" opacity="0.8"/>',
        f'<path d="{poly(ventral, False)}" fill="none" stroke="#A83840" stroke-width="2.4" stroke-linecap="round" opacity="0.4"/>',

def steam_wisp(cx, y0, height, width, bend):
    """Tapered vertical puff. y0 is the base; the wisp rises by `height`."""

        f'fill="none" stroke="#2A4574" stroke-width="3.5" stroke-linecap="round" opacity="0.65"/>',
        # Far rim (upper half of the ellipse).
        _rim_band(cx, cy, rx, ry, 16, near=False),

def _rim_band(cx, cy, rx, ry, thickness, near=True):
    rxi = rx - thickness
    ryi = max(6, ry - thickness * 0.72)
    if near:
        # Lower half: left --clockwise--> right, back along the inner edge.
        d = (
            f"M{fmt(cx - rx)},{fmt(cy)} A{fmt(rx)},{fmt(ry)} 0 0 1 {fmt(cx + rx)},{fmt(cy)} "
            f"L{fmt(cx + rxi)},{fmt(cy)} A{fmt(rxi)},{fmt(ryi)} 0 0 0 {fmt(cx - rxi)},{fmt(cy)} Z"
        )
        red = (
            f"M{fmt(cx - rxi + 2)},{fmt(cy + 2)} A{fmt(rxi - 2)},{fmt(ryi - 2)} 0 0 1 "
            f"{fmt(cx + rxi - 2)},{fmt(cy + 2)}"
        )
    else:
        d = (
            f"M{fmt(cx - rx)},{fmt(cy)} A{fmt(rx)},{fmt(ry)} 0 0 0 {fmt(cx + rx)},{fmt(cy)} "
            f"L{fmt(cx + rxi)},{fmt(cy)} A{fmt(rxi)},{fmt(ryi)} 0 0 1 {fmt(cx - rxi)},{fmt(cy)} Z"
        )
        red = (
            f"M{fmt(cx - rxi + 2)},{fmt(cy)} A{fmt(rxi - 2)},{fmt(max(4, ryi - 2))} 0 0 0 "
            f"{fmt(cx + rxi - 2)},{fmt(cy)}"
        )
    return (
        f'<path d="{d}" fill="#FFF8F0"/>'
        f'<path d="{red}" fill="none" stroke="#C4473A" stroke-width="2.4" opacity="0.85"/>'
    )


def _noodle_strand(x0, y, length, amp, waves, phase, sag, width, color):
    pts = []
    n = 22
    for i in range(n + 1):
        t = i / n
        x = x0 + length * t
        yy = y + math.sin(t * waves * math.tau + phase) * amp + math.sin(t * math.pi) * sag
        pts.append((x, yy))
    return (
        f'<path d="{poly(pts, False)}" fill="none" stroke="{color}" stroke-width="{fmt(width)}" '
        f'stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"/>'
    )

def _naruto(cx, cy):
    # Pink spiral fish cake, standing nearly face-on.
    pts = []
    turns, n = 2.15, 70
    for i in range(n + 1):
        t = i / n
        a = t * turns * math.tau
        r = 2 + t * 13
        pts.append((cx + r * math.cos(a), cy + r * math.sin(a) * 0.92))
    return (
        f'<ellipse cx="{fmt(cx)}" cy="{fmt(cy)}" rx="20" ry="18" fill="#FFFCFA" stroke="#F3C2D0" stroke-width="1"/>'
        f'<circle cx="{fmt(cx)}" cy="{fmt(cy)}" r="16" fill="none" stroke="#F4A2B8" stroke-width="3"/>'
        f'<path d="{poly(pts, False)}" fill="none" stroke="#F28BA8" stroke-width="3.2" stroke-linecap="round"/>'
    )

def lifted_noodles():
    """U-shaped strands pinched by the chopsticks, dripping back into the bowl."""
    tipx, tipy = 786, 778
    parts = []
    strands = [
        (-8, 6, 64, 2.0, "#E8D0A0", 6.4),
        (-2, 10, 96, 2.4, "#F8E7C4", 7.2),
        (4, 4, 118, 1.6, "#E2C890", 6.6),
        (0, 12, 78, 2.2, "#FFF3D8", 7.0),
        (6, 8, 102, 1.8, "#F3E0B0", 6.2),
        (-4, 2, 88, 2.6, "#EBD7A4", 7.4),
    ]
    for ox, oy, droop, wav, col, width in strands:
        pts = []
        n = 26
        x0, x1 = tipx - 7 + ox, tipx + 9 + ox
        y = tipy + oy
        for i in range(n + 1):
            t = i / n
            x = x0 + (x1 - x0) * t
            sag = math.sin(t * math.pi) * droop
            wave = math.sin(t * 6 * math.pi) * wav * math.sin(t * math.pi)
            pts.append((x, y + sag + wave))
        parts.append(
            f'<path d="{poly(pts, False)}" fill="none" stroke="{col}" stroke-width="{width}" '
            f'stroke-linecap="round"/>'
        )
    # Broth bead falling from the longest strand.
    dx, dy = tipx + 2, tipy + 104
    parts.append(
        f'<path d="M{fmt(dx)},{fmt(dy - 8)} C{fmt(dx - 5)},{fmt(dy - 2)} {fmt(dx - 4.5)},{fmt(dy + 5)} '
        f'{fmt(dx)},{fmt(dy + 8)} C{fmt(dx + 4.5)},{fmt(dy + 5)} {fmt(dx + 5)},{fmt(dy - 2)} {fmt(dx)},{fmt(dy - 8)} Z" '
        f'fill="#E39B2B"/>'
        f'<ellipse cx="{fmt(dx - 1.5)}" cy="{fmt(dy - 2)}" rx="1.6" ry="2.4" fill="#fff" opacity="0.65"/>'
    )
    return "".join(parts)

def lantern(cx, top, height, width, gid):
    rx, ry = width / 2, height / 2
    cy = top + ry + 10
    cap_w = width * 0.46
    parts = [
        f'<line x1="{fmt(cx)}" y1="250" x2="{fmt(cx)}" y2="{fmt(cy - ry - 8)}" stroke="#2A1C18" stroke-width="2"/>',
        f'<ellipse cx="{fmt(cx)}" cy="{fmt(cy)}" rx="{fmt(rx + 18)}" ry="{fmt(ry)}" fill="#FFB03A" opacity="0.45" filter="url(#glow)">'
        f'<animate attributeName="opacity" values="0.32;0.55;0.4;0.52" dur="{3.2 + (gid % 3) * 0.4}s" repeatCount="indefinite"/>'
        f"</ellipse>",
        ellipse(cx, cy, rx, ry, "url(#lantern)"),
        ellipse(cx - rx * 0.28, cy - ry * 0.08, rx * 0.28, ry * 0.62, "#FFD7A8", ' opacity="0.28"'),
    ]
    # Ribs.
    rib = [f'<clipPath id="lan{gid}"><ellipse cx="{fmt(cx)}" cy="{fmt(cy)}" rx="{fmt(rx - 1)}" ry="{fmt(ry - 1)}"/></clipPath>', f'<g clip-path="url(#lan{gid})">']
    for i in range(1, 8):
        yy = cy - ry + (2 * ry) * i / 8
        rib.append(
            f'<ellipse cx="{fmt(cx)}" cy="{fmt(yy)}" rx="{fmt(rx)}" ry="3.2" fill="none" stroke="#9E221C" stroke-width="2" opacity="0.55"/>'
        )
    rib.append(
        f'<line x1="{fmt(cx)}" y1="{fmt(cy - ry)}" x2="{fmt(cx)}" y2="{fmt(cy + ry)}" stroke="#7A1A16" stroke-width="1.4" opacity="0.45"/>'
    )
    rib.append("</g>")
    parts.append("".join(rib))
    parts.append(
        f'<rect x="{fmt(cx - cap_w / 2)}" y="{fmt(cy - ry - 8)}" width="{fmt(cap_w)}" height="12" rx="3" fill="#1A1214"/>'
    )
    parts.append(
        f'<rect x="{fmt(cx - cap_w / 2)}" y="{fmt(cy + ry - 4)}" width="{fmt(cap_w)}" height="12" rx="3" fill="#1A1214"/>'

    # Tassel.
    parts.append(
        f'<path d="M{fmt(cx)},{fmt(cy + ry + 8)} l-7,16 h14 Z" fill="#E6B14A"/>'
    )
    return "".join(parts)

def build():
    # Order is back to front. Tentacles are split so each one can tuck
    # behind the thing it actually passes behind.
    sections = [
        ("sky", sky),
        ("awning", awning),
        ("stall", posts_and_interior),
        ("menu", menu_and_shelf),
        ("straps", chef_body_back),
        ("head", chef_head),
        ("hat", hat),
        ("apron", apron),
        ("noren", noren),
        ("counter", counter),
        ("pot", pot_and_ladle),
        ("bottles", bottles),
        ("arms-mid", tentacles),
        ("bowl-back", bowl_back),
        ("toppings", toppings),
        ("lifted", lifted_noodles),
        ("near-rim", near_rim),
        ("chopsticks", chopsticks),
        ("chopstick-arm", tentacle_chopsticks),
        ("scallion-arm", tentacle_scallion),
        ("drape-arm", tentacle_drape),
        ("wave", tentacle_wave),
        ("steam", steam),
        ("lanterns", lambda: lantern(132, 268, 150, 74, 1) + lantern(1066, 268, 150, 74, 2)),
        ("ground", ground),
    ]
    body = []
    for name, fn in sections:
        body.append(f"<!-- {name} -->")
        body.append(fn())

def fmt(v):
    if isinstance(v, str):
        return v
    s = f"{float(v):.1f}"
    return s[:-2] if s.endswith(".0") else s


def poly(pts, close=True):
    if not pts:
        return ""
    cmds = [f"M{fmt(pts[0][0])} {fmt(pts[0][1])}"]
    cmds.extend(f"L{fmt(x)} {fmt(y)}" for x, y in pts[1:])
    if close:
        cmds.append("Z")
    return "".join(cmds)


def catmull(points, samples=12):
    if len(points) < 2:
        return list(points)
    p = [points[0]] + list(points) + [points[-1]]
    out = []
    for i in range(1, len(p) - 2):
        p0, p1, p2, p3 = p[i - 1], p[i], p[i + 1], p[i + 2]
        for s in range(samples):
            t = s / samples
            t2 = t * t
            t3 = t2 * t
            x = 0.5 * (
                (2 * p1[0])
                + (-p0[0] + p2[0]) * t
                + (2 * p0[0] - 5 * p1[0] + 4 * p2[0] - p3[0]) * t2
                + (-p0[0] + 3 * p1[0] - 3 * p2[0] + p3[0]) * t3
            )
            y = 0.5 * (
                (2 * p1[1])
                + (-p0[1] + p2[1]) * t
                + (2 * p0[1] - 5 * p1[1] + 4 * p2[1] - p3[1]) * t2
                + (-p0[1] + 3 * p1[1] - 3 * p2[1] + p3[1]) * t3
            )
            out.append((x, y))
    out.append(points[-1])
    return out


def resample(pts, step=4.2):
    if len(pts) < 2:
        return list(pts)
    seglen = []
    total = 0.0
    for i in range(1, len(pts)):
        L = math.hypot(pts[i][0] - pts[i - 1][0], pts[i][1] - pts[i - 1][1])
        seglen.append(L)
        total += L
    if total < step:
        return [pts[0], pts[-1]]
    out = [pts[0]]
    target = step
    seg_i = 0
    acc = 0.0
    while target < total - 0.01 and seg_i < len(seglen):
        while seg_i < len(seglen) and acc + seglen[seg_i] < target:
            acc += seglen[seg_i]
            seg_i += 1
        if seg_i >= len(seglen) or seglen[seg_i] < 1e-8:
            break
        local = (target - acc) / seglen[seg_i]
        x0, y0 = pts[seg_i]
        x1, y1 = pts[seg_i + 1]
        out.append((x0 + (x1 - x0) * local, y0 + (y1 - y0) * local))
        target += step
    out.append(pts[-1])
    return out


def append_spiral(pts, turns=0.7, radius=26, clockwise=True, samples=26):
    """Hook the tip into a tightening curl whose start tangent matches the arm."""
    if len(pts) < 2 or radius <= 1:
        return pts
    x1, y1 = pts[-1]
    x0, y0 = pts[-2]
    direction = math.atan2(y1 - y0, x1 - x0)
    sign = 1.0 if clockwise else -1.0
    raw = []
    for i in range(samples + 1):
        t = i / samples
        theta = sign * t * turns * math.tau
        r = radius * (1 - t * 0.86)
        raw.append((r * math.cos(theta) - radius, r * math.sin(theta)))
    tang = math.atan2(raw[1][1] - raw[0][1], raw[1][0] - raw[0][0])
    rot = direction - tang
    ca, sa = math.cos(rot), math.sin(rot)
    out = list(pts)
    for x, y in raw[1:]:
        out.append((x1 + x * ca - y * sa, y1 + x * sa + y * ca))
    return out


def normals(pts):
    n = len(pts)
    raw = []
    for i in range(n):
        if i == 0:
            dx = pts[1][0] - pts[0][0]
            dy = pts[1][1] - pts[0][1]
        elif i == n - 1:
            dx = pts[-1][0] - pts[-2][0]
            dy = pts[-1][1] - pts[-2][1]
        else:
            dx = pts[i + 1][0] - pts[i - 1][0]
            dy = pts[i + 1][1] - pts[i - 1][1]
        L = math.hypot(dx, dy) or 1.0
        raw.append((-dy / L, dx / L))
    fixed = [raw[0]]
    for i in range(1, n):
        nx, ny = raw[i]
        if nx * fixed[-1][0] + ny * fixed[-1][1] < 0:
            nx, ny = -nx, -ny
        fixed.append((nx, ny))
    cur = fixed
    for _ in range(2):
        nxt = [cur[0]]
        for i in range(1, n - 1):
            x = cur[i - 1][0] + cur[i][0] + cur[i + 1][0]
            y = cur[i - 1][1] + cur[i][1] + cur[i + 1][1]
            L = math.hypot(x, y) or 1.0
            nxt.append((x / L, y / L))
        nxt.append(cur[-1])
        cur = nxt
    return cur


def width_profile(n, base, tip, bulge=0.08):
    ws = []
    for i in range(n):
        t = i / (n - 1) if n > 1 else 0.0
        w = tip + (base - tip) * (1 - t) ** 0.76
        w *= 1 + bulge * math.sin(math.pi * t)
        ws.append(w)
    return ws


def semi_cap(tip, normal, width, forward=True, n=8):
    nx, ny = normal
    dx, dy = (ny, -nx) if forward else (-ny, nx)
    hw = width / 2
    pts = []
    for i in range(1, n):
        a = math.pi * i / n
        pts.append(
            (
                tip[0] + hw * (math.cos(a) * nx + math.sin(a) * dx),
                tip[1] + hw * (math.cos(a) * ny + math.sin(a) * dy),
            )
        )
    return pts


def ribbon_edges(pts, widths, norms):
    left, right = [], []
    for (x, y), (nx, ny), w in zip(pts, norms, widths):
        hw = w / 2
        left.append((x + nx * hw, y + ny * hw))
        right.append((x - nx * hw, y - ny * hw))
    cap = semi_cap(pts[-1], norms[-1], widths[-1], True)
    base = semi_cap(pts[0], norms[0], widths[0], False)
    outline = left + cap + list(reversed(right)) + list(reversed(base))
    return outline, left, right


def sucker_positions(pts, widths, norms, side, rows):
    found = []
    dist = 0.0
    next_at = max(8.0, widths[0] * 0.55)
    next_row2 = next_at + 9
    for i in range(1, len(pts) - 1):
        dist += math.hypot(pts[i][0] - pts[i - 1][0], pts[i][1] - pts[i - 1][1])
        t = i / (len(pts) - 1)
        w = widths[i]
        r = max(2.4, w * 0.268)
        spacing = max(r * 2.2, 7.5)
        nx, ny = norms[i]
        if 0.07 < t < 0.9 and dist >= next_at:
            found.append(
                (
                    pts[i][0] + side * nx * w * 0.04,
                    pts[i][1] + side * ny * w * 0.04,
                    r,
                )
            )
            next_at = dist + spacing
        if rows >= 2 and w > 18 and 0.12 < t < 0.86 and dist >= next_row2:
            r2 = r * 0.86
            found.append(
                (
                    pts[i][0] + side * nx * w * 0.30,
                    pts[i][1] + side * ny * w * 0.30,
                    r2,
                )
            )
            next_row2 = dist + max(r2 * 2.35, 8)
    return found


def sucker_mark(cx, cy, r):
    return (
        f'<circle cx="{fmt(cx)}" cy="{fmt(cy)}" r="{fmt(r)}" fill="#F3B2A6"/>'
        f'<circle cx="{fmt(cx)}" cy="{fmt(cy)}" r="{fmt(r * 0.70)}" fill="#D25A56"/>'
        f'<circle cx="{fmt(cx)}" cy="{fmt(cy)}" r="{fmt(r * 0.36)}" fill="#9E333C"/>'
        f'<circle cx="{fmt(cx - r * 0.28)}" cy="{fmt(cy - r * 0.30)}" r="{fmt(r * 0.16)}" fill="#fff" opacity="0.8"/>'
    )


def draw_tentacle(points, base, tip, fill, sucker_side=1, rows=1, spiral=None, bulge=0.08):
    pts = catmull(points, 11)
    if spiral:
        pts = append_spiral(pts, **spiral)
    pts = resample(pts, 4.0)
    if len(pts) < 4:
        return ""
    ws = width_profile(len(pts), base, tip, bulge)
    norms = normals(pts)
    outline, left, right = ribbon_edges(pts, ws, norms)
    dorsal = right if sucker_side > 0 else left
    ventral = left if sucker_side > 0 else right
    parts = [
        f'<path d="{poly(outline)}" fill="{fill}"/>',
        f'<path d="{poly(dorsal, False)}" fill="none" stroke="#FFD5CB" stroke-width="3.4" stroke-linecap="round" opacity="0.8"/>',
        f'<path d="{poly(ventral, False)}" fill="none" stroke="#A83840" stroke-width="2.4" stroke-linecap="round" opacity="0.4"/>',
    ]
    for cx, cy, r in sucker_positions(pts, ws, norms, sucker_side, rows):
        parts.append(sucker_mark(cx, cy, r))
    if DEBUG:
        parts.append(
            f'<path d="{poly(pts, False)}" fill="none" stroke="#00e5ff" stroke-width="1"/>'
        )
    return "".join(parts)


def text_glyph(key, x, baseline, fill, anchor="left", dx=0, dy=0, opacity=1):
    d, w, _a = GLYPHS[key]
    if anchor == "center":
        x -= w / 2
    elif anchor == "right":
        x -= w
    op = "" if opacity == 1 else f' opacity="{opacity}"'
    return (
        f'<path d="{d}" fill="{fill}" fill-rule="evenodd"{op} '
        f'transform="translate({fmt(x + dx)} {fmt(baseline + dy)})"/>'
    )


def ellipse(cx, cy, rx, ry, fill, extra=""):

def steam_wisp(cx, y0, height, width, bend):
    """Tapered vertical puff. y0 is the base; the wisp rises by `height`."""
    pts = []
    n = 18
    for i in range(n + 1):
        t = i / n
        y = y0 - height * t
        x = cx + math.sin(t * math.pi) * bend + math.sin(t * math.tau) * bend * 0.25
        pts.append((x, y))
    ws = [math.sin(i / n * math.pi) * width for i in range(n + 1)]
    ws[0] = 0.8
    ws[-1] = 0.6
    norms = normals(pts)
    outline, _, _ = ribbon_edges(pts, ws, norms)
    return poly(outline)

def _rim_band(cx, cy, rx, ry, thickness, near=True):
    rxi = rx - thickness
    ryi = max(6, ry - thickness * 0.72)
    if near:
        # Lower half: left --clockwise--> right, back along the inner edge.

def build():
    # Order is back to front. Tentacles are split so each one can tuck
    # behind the thing it actually passes behind.
    sections = [
        ("sky", sky),
        ("awning", awning),
        ("stall", posts_and_interior),

<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 {W} {H}" width="{W}" height="{H}" role="img">

{defs()}
</defs>
{"".join(body)}
</svg>
'''


def main():

    print(f"wrote {OUT} ({len(svg)} bytes)")


if __name__ == "__main__":

# Verify sips crop offset direction by sampling a pixel via png
import struct, zlib
def read_png(path):
    data = open(path,'rb').read()
    assert data[:8] == b'\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n'
    pos = 8
    w=h=None
    idat=b''
    while pos < len(data):
        n = struct.unpack('>I', data[pos:pos+4])[0]
        typ = data[pos+4:pos+8]
        chunk = data[pos+8:pos+8+n]
        if typ == b'IHDR':
            w,h = struct.unpack('>II', chunk[:8])
        elif typ == b'IDAT':
            idat += chunk
        elif typ == b'IEND':
            break
        pos += 12+n
    raw = zlib.decompress(idat)
    # assume RGBA or RGB
    return w,h,raw
for p in ['/tmp/svgpreview/face.png','/tmp/svgpreview/menu.png']:
    w,h,_=read_png(p)
    print(p, w, h)
